name: 3d-perspective-text
title: 3D Perspective Text
description: A large block of bold orange copy is tilted back in strong 3D perspective on a dark stage. As the page scrolls the text lifts and flattens toward the reader, with a small hint above telling you to scroll.
use: A manifesto or intro should feel cinematic, with a paragraph that pulls the reader in as they scroll.
avoid: It needs a very tall scroll parent and spreads the paragraph over many screens, so it cannot be skimmed.
a11y: The tilt and smooth scrolling ignore reduced-motion, and a 300vh pinned section spreads the paragraph over several screens. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark full-width stage holding a wide paragraph of heavy orange text set in a deep backward tilt, the top lines larger and the lower ones compressed. A tiny two-line hint sits above centre with a thin vertical rule hanging from it.
behaves: The block is pinned while the page scrolls, its backward tilt easing from steep toward nearly flat as progress advances. A gradient fades the bottom edge into the dark as the lines rise into view.
customise: Only the paragraph text and the hint line are props; the orange, type size, scroll length and the 3D tilt are fixed in the source.
weight: light: One text node transformed from scroll progress, plus a smooth-scroll wrapper.
demo: A paragraph beginning "Every great interface starts as a sentence" and the hint "scroll down to see".
issues: The first frame is almost empty apart from the scroll hint.
The deep tilt clips lines at the edges mid-scroll.
No reduced-motion handling guards the scroll transform.
polishWhy: Bold, coherent scroll typography; edges clip and the opening frame looks empty.
